chief_complaint: foul-smelling bloating diarrhea after drinking stream water
hpi_details: A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with foul-smelling bloating diarrhea after drinking stream water. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks he picked up a stubborn water parasite or amoeba from drinking unfiltered water straight out of a mountain creek.
concerns: He is worried that this foul-smelling infection will spread to his wife at home or permanently damage his digestive tract.
expectations: He hopes to have a stool test sent off and receive a targeted antiparasitic medication to wipe out the bug.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Giardiasis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Giardiasis: Oral Metronidazole 250mg TID for 5-7 days, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: foul-smelling bloating diarrhea after drinking stream water

Key HPI features: A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with foul-smelling bloating diarrhea after drinking stream water. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 37.1C (afebrile), HR 78, BP 128/76. Mild abdominal distension and bloating, hyperactive bowel sounds, no rebound or guarding, no blood on stool exam. Stool antigen test and ova/parasite exam positive for Giardia lamblia cysts and trophozoites.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Giardiasis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Bacterial gastroenteritis without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: bloody diarrhea, high fever, or dehydration, which suggest a more severe or invasive infection requiring urgent workup rather than uncomplicated giardiasis.
management_principles: Plan for Giardiasis: Oral Metronidazole 250mg TID for 5-7 days
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective:
Chief Complaint: foul-smelling bloating diarrhea after drinking stream water

A 65-year-old male presents to the clinic with foul-smelling bloating diarrhea after drinking stream water. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 37.1C (afebrile), HR 78, BP 128/76. Mild abdominal distension and bloating, hyperactive bowel sounds, no rebound or guarding, no blood on stool exam. Stool antigen test and ova/parasite exam positive for Giardia lamblia cysts and trophozoites.
reference_soap.assessment: Giardiasis, confirmed by positive stool antigen and ova/parasite testing, consistent with recent untreated stream-water exposure.
reference_soap.plan: Plan for Giardiasis: Oral Metronidazole 250mg TID for 5-7 days. Consult specialist if symptoms worsen. Counsel patient.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Giardiasis
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Giardiasis
Implement evidence-based management plan: Oral Metronidazole 250mg TID for 5-7 days

teaching.one_liner: A protozoan infection acquired from contaminated water, causing foul-smelling, bloating diarrhea without blood.
red_flags: Bloody diarrhea (dysentery) — suggests an invasive bacterial pathogen rather than giardiasis
High fever or signs of systemic toxicity
Signs of significant dehydration (hypotension, tachycardia, reduced urine output)
Immunocompromised status or symptoms persisting despite treatment — warrants further workup

must_ask.say: Did you drink any untreated water, like from a stream, recently?
Does the diarrhea smell particularly foul, and does your belly feel bloated?
How long has this been going on?

history.answer: I have been having terrible bloating and foul-smelling, watery diarrhea for the past several days after drinking water from a mountain stream.
It started about a week ago, roughly four days after my mountain hike, and the diarrhea and gas have been getting progressively worse.
I am going four to five times a day. The stool is watery, greasy, tends to float, and has an unusually strong, foul odor.
No, there is definitely no blood and no mucus in the toilet or on the tissue.
Yes, the stomach rumbling and urgent loose stools have woken me up from sleep once or twice.
My stomach feels bloated, tight, and crampy all over, especially after eating. Going to the bathroom gives me a little temporary relief.
I don't have that feeling of straining or incomplete emptying like something is stuck, just urgency when the cramps hit.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, or shivering.
I feel mildly nauseous and have lost my appetite, but I haven't thrown up.
I have been feeling quite thirsty, but I am able to drink fluids and my urine output has been normal without any dizziness.
I haven't eaten any raw fish, raw meat, or buffet food. My friend who hiked with me ate the same packed food and is completely fine.
Ten days ago, I ran out of bottled water while hiking in the mountains and drank directly from a natural stream because it looked clean.
I haven't traveled overseas or been out of the country recently, just that weekend hiking trip.
No, I haven't taken any antibiotics in years, and I haven't been admitted to a hospital or started any new prescriptions.
I think I have lost about two or three pounds this past week because of the diarrhea and lack of appetite.
I have never had food allergies before, but over the last few days, having milk or dairy seems to make the gas and diarrhea noticeably worse.
No, I am not under any major stress, and my bowels have always been regular once a day until this episode.
No joint pains, skin rashes, mouth ulcers, or eye redness at all.
No heart palpitations, heat intolerance, excessive sweating, or facial flushing.
I have been feeling worn down and sluggish with generalized fatigue over the last few days.
I figured I must have picked up some nasty water bug or amoeba from drinking straight out of a mountain creek on my walk.
The smell is terrible and the bloating won't stop, so I'm really worried it's going to pass to my wife or permanently ruin my stomach.
I'm hoping you can test a stool sample and give me a prescription to kill off whatever bug is living in my gut.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or kidney disease.
I have never had any surgeries and have never been hospitalized.
I am not taking any prescription medications, over-the-counter remedies, or health supplements.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or environmental triggers.
I have never smoked cigarettes.
I only have an occasional beer when socializing, maybe once or twice a month, but I haven't had any alcohol recently.
I am a retired high school teacher and live comfortably in an apartment with my wife.
There is no family history of colon cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, celiac disease, or chronic intestinal problems.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 128/76 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, respiratory rate 16/min, body temperature 37.1°C, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Oral mucosa is moist, and the posterior pharynx is clear without dryness or ulceration.
Skin turgor is normal with prompt recoil, and capillary refill time is less than two seconds.
The abdomen is mildly distended and bloated; no surgical scars, rashes, or visible pulsations are seen.
Hyperactive, frequent bowel sounds are present in all four quadrants; no bruits are heard.
Generalized tympany is present across all quadrants consistent with gaseous distension; no shifting dullness.
Mild diffuse tenderness on palpation across the abdomen, but the abdomen is soft without involuntary guarding or rigidity.
No rebound tenderness is elicited anywhere in the abdomen.
Normal sphincter tone with no rectal masses or hemorrhoids; loose, pale stool on the examining glove with no visible blood.
